import numpy as np

np.random.seed(42)
n_flips = 100000
flips = np.random.binomial(1, 0.5, n_flips)

running_avg = np.cumsum(flips) / np.arange(1, n_flips + 1)

true_p = 0.5

error = np.abs(running_avg - true_p)

tolerance = 0.01
for i in range(n_flips - 1, -1, -1):
    if error[i] > tolerance:
        convergence_point = i + 2
        break
else:
    convergence_point = 1

sample_sizes = [10, 100, 1000, 10000, 100000]
errors_at_sizes = {}
for size in sample_sizes:
    sample = np.random.binomial(1, 0.5, size)
    errors_at_sizes[size] = abs(np.mean(sample) - true_p)

n = 10000
k = 2
sigma = np.sqrt(true_p * (1 - true_p) / n)
chebyshev_bound = 1 / k**2

n_simulations = 10000
sample_means = np.mean(np.random.binomial(1, 0.5, (n_simulations, n)), axis=1)
empirical_prob = np.mean(np.abs(sample_means - true_p) >= k * sigma)

print(f"Final running average: {running_avg[-1]:.4f}")
print(f"Convergence point (within {tolerance}): {convergence_point}")
for size, err in errors_at_sizes.items():
    print(f"Error at n={size}: {err:.4f}")
print(f"Chebyshev bound: {chebyshev_bound:.4f}")
print(f"Empirical probability: {empirical_prob:.4f}")
